Assess the impact of Einstein’s work on our understanding of the nature of light.
Einstein’ work had a very significant impact on our understanding of the nature of light.
Prior to Einstein light was thought to be wave but Einstein’s work to explain the photoelectric effect
reconceptualised light as a quantised particle.
The photoelectric effect is the emission of electrons from the surface of a metal when exposed to light. It had
been observed that only light above a certain frequency would cause this to happen. Einstein explained this by
suggesting that light consisted of particles (photons)whose energy was proportional to their frequency and that
electrons could only observe all or nothing from a single photon.
Einstiens theory of special relativity postulated that the speed of light was constant. He was only able to show
this mathematically and explain it with thought experiments but ultimately he was proven correct with
significant experimental evidence.
Overall Einstien work was critical in changing our understanding of light.

Referring to the work of Bohr and Rutherford in atomic physics, discuss how scientists use
experimental observation and physical principles to improve scientific models.
Models are constructed to explain observations and create further predictions of behaviour. Bohr and
Rutherford developed their respective models by using physical principals to explain experimental
observations.
Gieger/Marsden fired alpha particles at thin gold and detected motion with a fluorescent screen.
Observations: most passed straight through some slight deflections and some bounced backward.
Rutherford understanding the principals of electrostatic repulsion (and elastic collisions) explained these results by
developing a model that consisted of a positively charged nucleus orbited by negatively charged electrons. The
dense positive nucleus accounting for the electrostatic repulsion of the alpha particles. (pic would be good)
Bohr could not account for the stability of the Rutherfords orbit because he understood the physical principal that
moving charged particles radiate energy and should therefore lose energy. To explain this and improve upon
Rutherford’s model he proposed that the electrons exist in discrete energy level which don’t radiate energy. These
electrons still orbited a positive nucleus. (pic would be good)In order to explain the experimentally observed
emission spectra of hydrogen Bohr adopted the newly proposed physical principal of quantised energy to suggest
that electrons move form one level to the next by absorbing/emitting a quanta of energy.
